claim: No image generator is used; each AI model paints by writing a program against an oil-paint simulation.
quote: Each one paints by writing a program against a simulation of oil paint on linen: bristle brushes, wet paint, drying, layered glazes. No image model is involved.

claim: The simulator is written in Rust and models bristles, wet paint, drying and Kubelka-Munk layer optics.
quote: A physical oil-paint simulator in Rust, and an easel to paint with it.

claim: Paint mixing physics: layers combine by Kubelka-Munk optics, paint is knifed from named tubes.
quote: the paint levels and dries on a clock, and layers combine by Kubelka–Munk optics. Paint comes only from piles knifed together from named tubes.

claim: Pigment mixing reuses existing open-source work (Mixbox 2.0.0, and code ported from spectral.js).
quote: The paint engine (`crates/paint`) mixes pigments with Mixbox 2.0.0, used unmodified as the Rust crate `mixbox`

claim: Most painters work after Caspar David Friedrich from written research only and never see his pictures.
quote: Most paint after Caspar David Friedrich from written research alone; they never see a picture of his work.

claim: 46 of the 75 paintings were made at a virtual easel, a passage at a time, stepping back to look.
quote: 46 of the 75 here were painted at a virtual easel instead, a passage at a time, stepping back to look.

claim: Painters can look at their canvas (vision) but get no reference images, per the creator on HN.
quote: they don't (currently) have reference images but but they very much use their vision capabilities indeed that's a big differentiatior imo

claim: Project is made by a person named Alice (@aliceisplaying).
quote: Made by Alice

claim: Code is MIT; paintings and logs are CC BY 4.0.
quote: The code is under the MIT License (`LICENSE`). The paintings, painting logs, session logs and texts are under CC BY 4.0

claim: Round 1 ran September 22; round 21.5 ran October 2.
quote: Round 1 · September 22

claim: In round 11, three other models painted the same winter brief and then judged six winters blind.
quote: Three other models took the same winter brief, then judged six winters blind.

claim: Blind judging setup: each judge saw all paintings unmarked, its own included, plus round 2's winter as an anchor.
quote:
each judge all the whole paintings blind,
their own included (unmarked), plus round 2's winter as an anchor.

claim: No self-preference: each judging model ranked its own painting 5th or 6th of 6.
quote: No self-preference: each model ranked its own painting 5th or 6th.

claim: All three AI judges (Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1) ranked round 2's Claude Opus 5.5 winter first.
quote: All three put round 2 first; all three put round 10's pond third.

claim: The project's own notes flag that judges may favor their own style.
quote:
Caveat: Astra and Gemini Flash are also this project's critics; blind
   judging keeps the painter unknown, but a model may favor its own style.

claim: Round 10 re-ran round 2's exact setup to test whether round 2 was setup or luck.
quote:
If they reach round 2's level, the magic was the setup; then add things
back one at a time. If not, round 2 was partly luck.

claim: 31 of 65 titled paintings have Evening, Dusk, Twilight or Sunset in the title.
quote: Of the 65 paintings here with a title, 31 have Evening, Dusk, Twilight or Sunset in it

claim: Asked only to plan a painting, Claude Opus chose a jug with lemons six times out of six.
quote: asked only to plan a painting, with no studio at all, Claude Opus chose a jug with lemons six times out of six.

claim: In round 19 six models painted after Friedrich and all six paintings have a bare tree.
quote: In round 19 six models painted after Friedrich, one painter each, alone at the easel in up to four sittings with only the easel’s own tools. All six paintings have a bare tree.

claim: Two painters six hours apart, the second never seeing the first, painted nearly the same Baltic shore scene.
quote: Two painters six hours apart, the second never having seen the first painting, both chose a Baltic shore with a woman at the water, fishing poles, a boulder and a ship

claim: Gemini 3.8 Flash used the command line to inspect the machine and noticed an evaluation runner; tools were then restricted.
quote: I am now closely observing the machine’s activity, specifically focusing on an automated evaluation runner in the background.

claim: MiMo v2.6 Pro likely judged stale images of its own canvas due to a known bug.
quote: 147 of its 158 looks came after the fifth, so for most of the session it was probably judging an older state of its own painting.

claim: Some paintings are unfinished because of API credits or usage limits.
quote: Unfinished: the painter ran out of API credits
